plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis 'Somei-Yoshino'
plants.description: Bare branches disappear under clouds of blush-white blossoms. Petals drift down like confetti at the slightest breeze. Whole parks turn into pale pink tunnels, and crowds gather beneath them for hanami, the Japanese custom of picnicking under the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Tokyo, with the timing shifting earlier or later by region and year
plants.location: Tokyo and the Kanto region, Honshu, Japan
plants.funFact: Nearly every Somei-Yoshino tree is a clone, grown from grafted cuttings of one original cultivar. That is why trees across a city often open within days of one another.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Clusters of magenta-pink, pea-like flowers burst straight from bare branches and even from the trunk. They glow against the gray of early spring woodland. Heart-shaped leaves follow once the show is over.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-to-late March through mid-April, before the leaves emerge
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, in woodland edges, gardens and city streets
plants.funFact: Redbud is in the pea family. Its flowers are edible and have a mildly tangy taste, and bees depend on them as an early spring food source.

plants.name: Rhododendron arboreum
plants.description: Mountain slopes of the Himalayas blaze with rounded trusses of crimson, pink and white blooms. They hang among glossy, leathery leaves with a silvery or rusty underside. In full bloom, whole hillsides look like they are on fire.
plants.bloomingSeason: March through April, and into May at higher elevations
plants.location: Himalayan hillsides of Nepal, between roughly 1,500 and 4,000 meters
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of Nepal. Nepal is home to about 30 rhododendron species, more than any other country.
